notes: No transcript captured for the baseline, so the exact content and number of clarifying questions cannot be verified — only inferred from empty outputs + short timing.
Strong, consistent skill effect: with_skill 98% ± 4% vs baseline 17% ± 12% pass rate (delta +0.81) across all 4 evals. The skill is doing real work — baseline never approaches it.

GENUINE SKILL FINDING: file-upload-quick (with_skill) failed 'Covers 1-3 capabilities (quick depth)' — it produced 5 capabilities (CAP-01..05), exceeding the documented quick band of 1-3. The skill's depth-control for 'quick' may be too loose. Candidate for iteration.

HARNESS ARTIFACT (not a skill flaw): 'Document is written to ./solution-architect/{slug}.md' fails for BOTH configs because the eval harness redirects output to a workspace dir. This assertion is unsatisfiable under the harness and should be reworded (e.g. check the document is written to the prescribed path OR a designated output dir).

Non-discriminating assertions: the generic topic-coverage checks (signup, billing, payouts, dispute handling, buyer/seller-facing) pass for the baseline too — they don't isolate skill value. The discriminating signal lives in the structure (7 named sections), CAP-NN IDs, per-capability fields, WHAT-not-HOW discipline, and researcher/librarian delegation assertions, all of which the baseline fails wholesale.

WHAT-not-HOW is the clearest skill differentiator: every baseline run leaked implementation detail (Stripe Connect, Elasticsearch/Algolia, 3DS2/PSD2, magic bytes, object storage) while every with_skill run stayed at the capability level.

Verifiability gap: the 'checks existing knowledge via librarian before starting' assertion passes on stated intent — the librarian skill was unavailable in the harness, so the skill wrote a documented fallback rather than making a real tool call. The assertion can't tell a genuine search from a placeholder.

vague-idea-clarify baseline produced NO document (it triggered interactive clarifying questions and stopped), so its dialogue-behavior assertions are only inferable from empty-outputs+short-timing. Capturing the assistant's text for no-file runs would make these gradable on evidence.

Cost of the skill: +76s wall-clock and +17k tokens per run on average vs baseline — expected, since the skill produces a far more complete structured artifact. Worth it given the +0.81 pass-rate lift.
